name: Transfer Pricing
title: Transfer Pricing
answer: Transfer pricing concerns the prices charged between related entities within a multinational group for goods, services, intangibles, and financing. It determines how profit is allocated across tax jurisdictions, affecting corporate income tax liabilities and compliance with the arm's length principle. The scope includes documentation, benchmarking, intercompany agreements, and defense in audits or disputes. For AI-related businesses, transfer pricing increasingly covers data, algorithms, model training services, and cloud computing resources shared across borders.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Transfer pricing concerns the prices charged between related entities within a multinational group for goods, services, intangibles, and financing. It determines how profit is allocated across tax jurisdictions, affecting corporate income tax liabilities and compliance with the arm's length principle. The scope includes documentation, benchmarking, intercompany agreements, and defense in audits or disputes. For AI-related businesses, transfer pricing increasingly covers data, algorithms, model training services, and cloud computing resources shared across borders.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Transfer pricing work runs on enterprise resource planning systems, financial consolidation platforms, and specialized transfer pricing documentation software. Data is drawn from intercompany transaction ledgers, contracts, and comparable company databases. Many teams now use AI-assisted tools for benchmarking searches, document generation, and risk scoring, but core calculations still rely on spreadsheets and tax provision systems. The infrastructure must handle multi-currency, multi-entity data with audit trails.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners identify controlled transactions, perform functional and risk analysis, select the most appropriate transfer pricing method such as comparable uncontrolled price, resale price, cost plus, transactional net margin, or profit split, and benchmark against independent comparables. They prepare local and master files, and monitor outcomes against policy. AI methods are used to screen large comparable sets, classify intercompany transactions, and detect outliers, but the professional judgment on comparability adjustments remains with the tax team.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Transfer pricing is governed by OECD guidelines, country-by-country reporting rules, and local tax authority requirements. Risks include double taxation, penalties, and reputational exposure if prices are challenged. Documentation must show the provenance of data, the rationale for method selection, and the arm's length range. AI-generated outputs need human review because tax authorities require contemporaneous evidence and defensible positions, not black-box recommendations.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Transfer pricing is moving toward real-time monitoring of intercompany margins, automated documentation updates, and predictive risk scoring for audit selection. Tax authorities are using data analytics to compare taxpayer positions across industries, which pushes companies to maintain consistent global policies. For AI-intensive groups, new guidance is emerging on the valuation of data and intangible assets, and on how to allocate profit from machine learning models trained in multiple jurisdictions. The direction is more transparency, more granular data, and closer integration between tax, finance, and AI system logs.
